## Matagalpa in Nicaragua!

## Matagalpa: a land of coffee, revolutionary traditions and history!

Places worth visiting include Jinotega, home to what is considered the country's finest coffee; Estelí, the "city of revolutionary traditions" and a center of reforestation efforts; Matagalpa, the "Pearl of the North"; and the renowned Selva Negra ("Black Forest"), with its ancient evergreen tropical forests. In the village of Muy Muy Viejo ("Very, Very Old"), enormous stone statues, numerous decorated clay vessels and objects carved from jade have been found, evidence of one of the most remarkable pre-Columbian settlements in the Americas. The region also has many fascinating small towns, each with a character of its own.

## Matanzas: the "Venice of Cuba"

Matanzas is known for its peaceful atmosphere and five distinctive bridges spanning the Yumurí and San Juan rivers. These bridges have earned it the nickname "Venice of Cuba".

Set on the shore of a deep bay, the city became famous in the 19th century as the country's sugar capital. On the shady central square, Parque de la Libertad, stands the Pharmaceutical Museum (Museo Farmacéutico), a beautifully preserved pharmacy founded in 1882. Along the street heading east toward the harbor rises the Cathedral of San Carlos Borromeo, a neoclassical building currently undergoing restoration.

## Matanzas: a peaceful corner of Cuba

Matanzas is home to Latin America's largest area of karst caves, which are more than 40,000 years old. The Bellamar Caves, east of the city, are Cuba's oldest tourist attraction. The caves were discovered by chance. On a guided visit, you can descend into a large chamber filled with stalactites and stalagmites.

## Flower Festival and Botero sculptures: what to see in Medellín

Medellín is Colombia's second-largest city. Affluent residential neighborhoods alternate with slums, and the city is described as a home to both the popular singer Shakira and the drug lord Pablo Escobar.

Medellín has a pleasant climate and is known as the "Silver Bowl" because it is surrounded by seven picturesque hills. The city has plenty to offer visitors. Its colonial-era heritage includes the Basilica of Our Lady of Candelaria and the Metropolitan Cathedral, renowned as the largest brick church in South America.

Among the landmarks you will see are the Basilica of Our Lady of Candelaria and the Metropolitan Cathedral, while the botanical garden has a famous orchid collection. The annual Flower Festival takes place in Medellín in late July and early August. This colorful celebration opens with a parade of "caballeros", as thousands of horsemen ride through the city.

## A holiday in Medellín

Picturesque scenery along the Porce River, the green slopes of the mighty Andes, and modern architecture give this metropolis its distinctive appearance. Its urban districts blend into majestic mountains at an elevation of more than 1,500 meters. Expressive sculptures, art galleries, recreation areas, orchids, museums, art studios, cafés and restaurants offer visitors a remarkable variety of experiences. The combination of beautiful scenery and modern infrastructure draws increasing numbers of travelers to the city.
